summary: Procurement/legal review with Suncrest Health covering MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets, data residency and onboarding steps. Redwood AE/SE walked through proposed language and technical onboarding requirements. Customer highlighted SOC2/ISO evidence, KMS requirements, and need for on-prem/private deployment options for PHI. Agreed next steps: exchange redlines, share security artifacts, run a 2-week pilot with monitoring metrics and performance SLOs.
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-21 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45 min
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Rao (Redwood SE); Jordan Kim (Redwood CSM); Tom Alvarez (Suncrest Legal); Sam Rogers (Suncrest Procurement); Maya Patel (Suncrest Platform Eng); Lena Ortiz (Suncrest InfoSec); Dr. Elena Morris (Suncrest Product)

Summary (auto): Review of MSA and DPA redlines, SLA targets and procurement timeline; discussed data residency, encryption/KMS, audit logs, and pilot/onboarding steps.

00:00 Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out the time. quick round table?
00:08 Tom Alvarez: tom here legal, i'll focus on contract bits, quick heads up we have tight timelines for this quarter.
00:12 Sam Rogers: sam procurement, budget owner, main ask is pricing approval and payment terms.
00:18 Maya Patel: maya, platform eng. i'll be hands-on for the pilot and integration.
00:24 Lena Ortiz: lena, infosec, i'll own security questionnaire and SOC2 review.
00:30 Alex Chen: great, from redwood we have priya se on the line for technical q's and jordan csm for onboarding. ok we'll walk the doc and call out items.

02:05 Alex Chen: first item — MSA indemnity and liability caps. we proposed a standard cap at 3x fees or $5M whichever is greater, typical for our enterprise plans.
02:20 Tom Alvarez: tom - that's a starting point. for healthcare PHI exposure we may ask for carve outs or higher caps; also we need clearer breach notification timelines in DPA.
02:38 Priya Rao: (interject) on breach notification our platform emits audit logs, we can do 72 hours for notification but we also provide near-real-time alerting via webhook if you want.
02:50 Lena Ortiz: 72 hours is ok as baseline but for PHI we prefer 48. is that negotiable?
03:05 Alex Chen: we can propose 48 for critical incidents; i'll flag that in redlines.

05:10 Sam Rogers: pricing — we have internal approval cycles. can you confirm the committed dedicated capacity discounts and overage terms?
05:22 Alex Chen: yes, dedicated (reserved) pricing in the sheet: 20% off hosted rates for a 12mo commit, overage billed at a blended rate; i'll attach the exact table, and we can add ramp language.
05:36 Maya Patel: for the pilot we need clear SLOs — 99th percentile latency target and token throughput. can redwood provide a test harness?
05:50 Priya Rao: absolutely, we have a pilot runbook. for latency SLOs we typically target sub-200ms for short responses on dedicated pools; we'll share benchmark artifacts.
06:10 Maya Patel: sub-200ms sounds good — need metrics collection and tracing access.
06:18 Jordan Kim: we'll set up per-route dashboards and give access to your team during the pilot.

08:00 Tom Alvarez: data residency — Suncrest has a strict rule: PHI must stay in us-east-1 or on-prem. how does Redwood support region pinning or private deployment?
08:18 Priya Rao: Redwood Private supports VPC/on-prem deployment. for hosted tenants we can pin to a region and restrict backups — vanilla hosted may not meet PHI controls without a private account.
08:34 Lena Ortiz: do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM for key control?
08:40 Priya Rao: yes, we integrate with AWS KMS and can support customer-managed keys in private deployments; HSM integrations are possible with the enterprise package.
08:55 Tom Alvarez: okay we'll need that in the DPA and in the security annex.

11:20 Alex Chen: SLA language — uptime guarantees, credits, response times for P1/P2. we typically do 99.9% for dedicated with 24/7 support and defined credit tables.
11:34 Tom Alvarez: we need defined MTTR targets and a clear escalation path in the contract; also want legal to see how credits apply to multi-tenant outages.
11:45 Jordan Kim: escalation path — we'll include a 24/7 SE on-call for dedicated customers and a ticket + phone escalation ladder in the SLA.
11:58 Lena Ortiz: can you provide SOC2 Type II report and any pen test evidence?
12:06 Priya Rao: yes, we'll share SOC2 and recent penetration test summary (redacted) under an NDA.

14:40 Sam Rogers: procurement timeline — if we get redlines back quickly we can route to finance in two weeks but pricing sign-off may take 3 weeks. hope to onboard pilot early april.
14:55 Alex Chen: sounds reasonable — our target is pilot start by 2026-04-06 if approvals line up.

16:10 Maya Patel: technical note — network whitelisting and IP ranges for outbound connections, and VPC peering options for private deployments. we need sample network diagrams.
16:24 Priya Rao: will share sample diagrams and required firewall rules; pilot can be run with whitelisted egress to our dedicated ip range.

18:00 Tom Alvarez: DPA redlines — we want explicit data deletion language, retention windows, and audit log retention controls. also clarify subprocessors list.
18:18 Alex Chen: we'll provide subprocessors list and a standard 90-day deletion window for non-essential logs, with an option to extend retention if you request.
18:30 Lena Ortiz: for audit logs we prefer 1 year retention and an export mechanism for compliance.
18:40 Jordan Kim: export is supported — we'll add S3 export guidance in the runbook.

21:05 Maya Patel: integration hooks — we need function-calling like structured outputs and tool/call support; does Redwood support streaming and function-calls?
21:20 Priya Rao: yes streaming responses and structured tool calling supported; we'll include examples in the dev quickstart.

23:00 Tom Alvarez: indemnity and IP — we need clear ownership of customer data and outputs, non-assertion of IP claims on customer prompts.
23:18 Alex Chen: Redwood's standard is customer retains rights to their data and generated outputs; we'll make that explicit in the MSA.

25:30 Sam Rogers: on billing, do you support net-30 or net-45?
25:35 Alex Chen: standard is net-30; enterprise can request net-45 after credit review.
25:42 Sam Rogers: we'll flag that. also need PO process for procurement.

28:10 Lena Ortiz: security questionnaire — there are a few items around vulnerability disclosure and SSO. do you support SAML/SCIM?
28:22 Priya Rao: yes SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning supported; we'll send our SSO setup guide.
28:32 Lena Ortiz: good. also looking for logging hooks and SIEM integration.
28:40 Priya Rao: we have webhook and syslog export options; SIEM integrations are documented.

31:00 Tom Alvarez: one contractual item — backup and disaster recovery RTO/RPO expectations for private deployments?
31:10 Priya Rao: for private we can agree to RTO under 4 hours for critical services and RPO under 1 hour; we'll propose language but it depends on the deployment model.
31:28 Tom Alvarez: please capture that and we'll review.

34:00 Alex Chen: ok recap — action items: we'll send marked-up MSA/DPA with 48-hour breach proposal for critical incidents, add KMS language, include subprocessors list, SLA/escalation ladder and pilot runbook. Priya will share onboarding artifacts and network diagrams. Lena will finish the vendor questionnaire and coordinate security follow-up. Sam will push pricing approval.

36:12 Sam Rogers: quick question on pilot success criteria — what's reasonable?
36:20 Priya Rao: recommend 2-week pilot, measurable: latency p99 < 250ms for sample workloads, no more than 2% error rate, and stability at expected qps. also monitoring integration and dashboard access.
36:36 Maya Patel: agree, also validate cost per 1k tokens for production estimate.
36:44 Alex Chen: we'll provide estimated billing templates and a pilot cost worksheet.

39:00 Tom Alvarez: legal will circle back on indemnity and data residency redlines, we may propose paper edits in track changes.
39:10 Alex Chen: perfect — once we get redlines we'll triage and propose final language.

41:20 Jordan Kim: onboarding timeline summary — exchange redlines by 3/25, security follow-up 3/27, pilot start target 4/06.
41:30 Alex Chen: i'll email a consolidated packet after this call: marked MSA/DPA, SLA appendix, pilot runbook, SOC2 and pen-test artifacts (NDA gating for some).
41:40 Tom Alvarez: thanks, we'll try to get legal comments within the week.

44:10 Alex Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the documents and schedule the security deep dive next week. bye.
44:17 Meeting ended
